title: Pin Audit SARIF scanner and ruleset evidence
summary: Pin Audit SARIF scanner versions and the downloaded Semgrep ruleset, then embed their identities in SARIF and job summaries.
reason: Batch 190 remediates AUDIT-FIND-W10-008. Audit SARIF currently resolves broad scanner ranges and mutable p/default rules at run time, so repeated evidence for one commit is not attributable to fixed inputs.
behavior_before: The hosted lane installs ranged Ruff and Semgrep versions, scans directly with mutable p/default, and records no ruleset digest in SARIF provenance.
behavior_after: The hosted lane installs exact scanner versions, downloads p/default only through an order-independent semantic SHA-256 lock over the complete rule set, and records scanner and ruleset identities in both SARIF and job-summary evidence.
tests_added: Pinned ruleset download accepts only the exact canonical semantic SHA-256, treats rule-list ordering as non-semantic, detects rule-content changes, and never replaces an existing output on mismatch.
SARIF stamping verifies the emitted scanner version and records deterministic scanner/ruleset provenance.
Workflow contract rejects version ranges, direct remote ruleset scans, missing digest verification, and missing summary provenance.
manual_validation: Run focused provenance/audit tests, YAML parsing, Ruff, py_compile, exact remote ruleset semantic-digest preflight, generated checks, strict packet coverage, and git diff --check.
Rung 6 remains pending until the pinned workflow is committed, pushed, run twice at one SHA, and normalized SARIF/tool identities compare equal.

validation_gates.description: Exact Ruff and Semgrep versions plus an order-independent semantic SHA-256-verified Semgrep ruleset are enforced and recorded in SARIF/job-summary evidence.
evidence: Audit SARIF installs exact Ruff 0.16.1, Semgrep 1.172.0, and PyYAML 6.0.3 versions; ranged installs and direct --config p/default scanning are absent. YAML loading is lazy so the Ruff-only lane remains independent of the ruleset parser.

The workflow fetches p/default through the provenance helper, accepts only semantic SHA-256 49f8c900fbeacc43c9069d2c2f0d02b1923148d6de08e1383e4e930508194e85 using canonical-json-sorted-rules-v1, scans the verified RUNNER_TEMP file, verifies each emitted SARIF driver version, and stamps scanner/ruleset identity for summaries and artifacts.

Hosted runs 30785059036 and 30785315224 proved raw p/default bytes are request-variant: three raw hashes were observed while all 1,074 rule IDs and rule objects were identical and only list ordering changed. Sorting complete rule objects by unique non-empty id before canonical JSON hashing produced the same 49f8c900fbeacc43c9069d2c2f0d02b1923148d6de08e1383e4e930508194e85 digest for the retained old payload and fresh responses; any rule addition, removal, duplicate id, or content change fails closed before output publication.

Focused provenance and audit-workflow tests passed 16 tests covering raw-order variance, semantic changes, duplicate/invalid rule structures, fetch preservation, provenance stamping, and normalized SARIF comparison; the revision-local focused plus required generated-context suite passed 53 tests. A live semantic fetch accepted raw SHA-256 bda58064ceb7c650e0c28e0534f1c8503e2f5d74171ad28a5f9951e54f14753b as the same locked 49f8c900fbeacc43c9069d2c2f0d02b1923148d6de08e1383e4e930508194e85 rule set.

validation_gates.description: Focused tooling, workflow parsing, generated outputs, packet coverage, immutable evidence, and diff checks complete.
evidence: Bundled Ruff, exact Ruff 0.16.1, py_compile, YAML parsing, and ops/scripts/dev/check-github-audit-spine.ps1 passed for the isolated Batch 190 revision.

All 2,546 isolated source summaries, project/dependency indexes, 15 feature cards, duplicate-test report, and 98 dependency-atlas detail diagrams were regenerated and reached current generator output.
Change-packet JSON validation and strict isolated-worktree coverage passed with 1,201 valid packets.

The full AI postflight passed every applicable generated-map, schema, dependency, architecture, naming, lifecycle, Office, risky-file, marketecture, and inventory gate and exited 1 only for the unrelated pre-existing DOC005 warning at docs/reviews/comprehensive-production-audit-2026-07-19/evidence/BASELINE.md:15.

The first isolated commit-hook audit suite passed 14 of 16 checks and additionally surfaced the clean-baseline unallowlisted NO_PACKAGE_CYCLES edge mediapipeline.core.processes -> mediapipeline.core.queue; Batch 190 adds no core or desktop import, so that dependency finding and DOC005 are unrelated. The isolated checkout initially lacked the ignored bundled-runtime path required by the Python-lint hook; an ignored junction to the primary bundled runtime restored that prerequisite for the retry.
git diff --check exited 0 with line-ending warnings only and zero diagnostics; the isolated index remained unstaged during validation.

validation_gates.description: Two hosted Audit SARIF runs at one committed revision report identical tool identities and normalized SARIF.
evidence: Acceptance requires two Audit SARIF runs at the exact pushed Batch 190 head SHA, artifact download, and equality of audit_sarif_provenance digest-sarif output for each scanner including embedded provenance.

Push-triggered Audit SARIF run 30785059036 at fc4a19da359c16c5b4be8370edf196b8c3e7b534 completed Ruff successfully and failed closed before Semgrep scanning on raw digest dcfed68d8357bd5150f03cb6d72f5117884f0255fb6153d57ce9325ec8e9affa versus local a7eb740a484688c0ba24668bb5fb7fc9a8ebc04c8eae982230d75f2ad9094bbc.

Push-triggered run 30785315224 at 39ecac3a39c221712a18e1390a93808c1ac36e3e completed Ruff successfully and failed closed before Semgrep scanning when the next hosted raw response changed again to d099855b047d4ed70743ea4d2e41a96080d8309d4ff07ab6444f516684a35f3d, establishing that raw-byte pinning is invalid for this request-order-variant endpoint.

Push-triggered run 30785768809 at 266d14590a7f606b38f87bbd30f21d2aa6d515c3 reached the canonical semantic-lock implementation but failed before digest evaluation because hosted Python lacked PyYAML; the same top-level import also prevented Ruff provenance stamping. The follow-up makes YAML loading lazy and pins PyYAML 6.0.3 only in the Semgrep lane.

rollback_plan: Restore ranged scanner installs and direct p/default scanning, remove the provenance helper/tests, regenerate context, and revert this packet. No runtime or media behavior changes.
notes: The exact 2,000-token context slice and no-touch boundary were read. This is release/audit evidence tooling, not release-package contents or media behavior; representative real media is not required. The validation rung is Rung 6 two-run audit-evidence comparison. The isolated Batch 190 canary intentionally excludes the earlier uncommitted AUDIT-FIND-W10-007 adjudication changes, their helper/tests, and all unrelated primary-worktree changes. Scanner pins remain Ruff 0.16.1 and Semgrep 1.172.0, matching successful scheduled Audit SARIF run 30741529429 on 2026-08-02; PyYAML 6.0.3 is separately pinned for semantic ruleset parsing in the Semgrep lane. Pre-push and hosted checks proved semgrep.dev/c/p/default returns request-variant raw bytes because its 1,074 semantically identical rules are emitted in different list orders. The workflow therefore locks canonical-json-sorted-rules-v1 semantic SHA-256 49f8c900fbeacc43c9069d2c2f0d02b1923148d6de08e1383e4e930508194e85; arbitrary serialization order is accepted, while any rule-set or rule-content drift fails closed before scan evidence is accepted. Vendoring the compiled response was rejected because the Semgrep Rules License v1.0 does not permit distributing the rules. The fetched config is written under RUNNER_TEMP so it cannot become a scan target. Python impact: developer audit tooling only. User authorization to commit and push Batch 190 was received on 2026-08-03; no manual workflow dispatch is authorized.
